summary: Anna M. Shields is a scholar in sinology. She held posts at the University of Maryland, College Park (~2007–2015) and Princeton University (~2015), and taught Zhiyi Yang and Thomas James Mazanec.

Anna Madelyn Hennessey works in sinology and religious studies. She earned her PhD from the University of California, Santa Barbara (attested 2011), where she studied under doctoral supervisor William F. Powell.

Anna Sawerthal is a tibetologist. She completed an MA at the University of Vienna under Klaus-Dieter Mathes and Johanna Buß, and a PhD at the University of Heidelberg supervised by Birgit Kellner and Roland Wenzlhuemer.

Anna Seidel was a scholar of sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She studied at Munich, Hamburg, and under Maxime Kaltenmark and Rolf Alfred Stein. Her career included posts at EFEO (1969) and the Institut du Hōbōgirin (~1969–1991).

Anna Szabolcsi is a linguist who studied at Eötvös Loránd University and the Hungarian Academy of Sciences. She served at the Hungarian Academy of Sciences (~1976–1990), UCLA (~1990–1998), and New York University (~1998).
Anna-Pya Sjödin works in Indology and philosophy. She earned her PhD at Uppsala University in 2007, supervised by Gunilla Gren-Eklund, Eli Franco, Jonardon Ganeri, K. Venugopalan, and Toshihiro Wada.

Anne Carolyn Klein specializes in Buddhist studies, tibetology, and religious studies. Educated at Binghamton, Wisconsin-Madison, and Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins and traditional teachers, she served at Harvard and became Professor of Religious Studies at Rice University in ~1994.

Anne E. Monius was a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She studied under Diana L. Eck and Kausalya Hart at Harvard University, later teaching at the University of Virginia (1997–2002) and Harvard (from 2002).

Anne Feldhaus is an Indology and religious studies scholar. She studied at Manhattanville University and earned her doctorate at the University of Pennsylvania, later holding a professorship at Arizona State University beginning in 1981.
Anne Hardgrove works in history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied at Carleton College and the University of Michigan, and took up a post at the University of Texas at San Antonio in 2000.

Anne M. Blackburn is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. She completed graduate studies at the University of Chicago (~1991–1996) and served as Assistant Professor of Religion at Cornell University (~2001–2006).

Anne MacDonald works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and tibetology. She studied at the University of British Columbia under Shotaro Iida, and held positions at the University of Vienna (attested 2001–2008) and the Austrian Academy of Sciences (attested 2012).

Anne Nishimura Morse specializes in Japanology and history/archaeology. She completed her PhD at Harvard University under John M. Rosenfield and held posts at Smith College (1988–1989), Tokyo National Research Institute (1988), Nara (1996), and Kyoto (1998).

Anne Ruth Hansen works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and history/archaeology. She studied under Charles Hallisey and held an affiliation at the University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee (attested 2007).

Anne-Marie Blondeau is a scholar of tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under Rolf Alfred Stein and several traditional teachers, and held positions at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (attested 1982 and 2003).

Anne-Marie Esnoul was an Indology, philosophy, and religious studies scholar. She studied under Paul Masson-Oursel at the Faculty of Arts of Paris and EPHE, later holding posts at CNRS, Institut de civilisation indienne, and EPHE (~1963–1977).
Annegret Bollée was a linguist who pursued her studies at the University of Hamburg, Aix-Marseille University, and the University of Bonn (1969).

Annemarie Schimmel specialized in religious studies and Iranian/Central Asian studies. Educated at Berlin and Marburg under Hans Heinrich Schaeder and Friedrich Heiler, she held posts at Marburg, Ankara University (1954–1967), and Harvard University (1967–1992).

Annemarie von Gabain worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and sinology. She studied at the University of Berlin (~1920–1930), later teaching there (~1937–1945) and at the University of Hamburg (~1957–1966).

Annette Baier was a philosopher who studied at the University of Otago and Somerville College, Oxford. She held academic appointments at Carnegie Mellon University (~1969–1972) and the University of Pittsburgh (~1979–1995).
